summary.headline: Jash Engineering Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 17% YoY to Rs156 crore and PAT turned positive at about Rs5 crore; FY27 target Rs875 crore reiterated.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue of Rs156 crore, up about 17% YoY, with PAT moving from about minus Rs5 crore to plus Rs5 crore and gross and EBITDA margins both higher YoY. Management said shipments to Qatar, Singapore and other Middle East customers were held back (about Rs15 crore in total), so the quarter was below what management expected. Consolidated order book stands at Rs932 crore (India Rs293 crore, outside India Rs639 crore). Management reiterated FY27 revenue of Rs875 crore and PAT of about Rs100-105 crore, and said Rs1,500 crore revenue is targeted by 2031.

financial_highlights.change: PAT up significantly; standalone PAT margin about 13% in Q1

segments.name: Jash Engineering (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 21% YoY with significantly higher PAT; order book Rs559 crore. Management says standalone PAT margin is about 13% in Q1.

segments.name: Rodney Hunt (US)
segments.commentary: Order book Rs369 crore; management targets over $35-36 million revenue in FY27 with profitability, and expects an 8-9% PAT margin. Management called Q1 a 'first quarter blues' quarter. Management also said the order book is close to $40 million.

segments.name: Jash Process Equipment (ex-WesTech)
segments.commentary: Order book only Rs29 crore; management said Rs150-200 crore of orders were lost in the last three to four months and a full review is under way. Management called this entity a concern.

segments.name: Waterfront
segments.commentary: Revenue up marginally YoY but profit up on high-margin executed orders; management reiterated Rs5 million-plus revenue target with significant profit. Order book Rs34 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of Rs875 crore (India Rs320 crore; outside India Rs555 crore), reiterated; management said there is potential to go beyond this but size is premature until Q2 or Q3 results.
FY27 PAT of about Rs100-105 crore stated in closing remarks; separately, PAT margin of 13-14% described as achievable for the year, depending on geopolitics.
Rs1,500 crore revenue targeted by 2031; FY28 revenue guidance of about Rs1,025 crore mentioned.
Further tariff refund of about Rs7.5 crore pending, expected to be filed and resolved in FY27 after legal vetting.
Saudi Arabia plant: land expected by end of CY2026, plant ready by December 2027, operations by March 2028. US (Houston/Orange) plant: land already acquired, contractor being finalised.
capex_capacity: Foundry expansion and gate and valve manufacturing expansion commissioned in Q1 FY27; management says capacity is up about 30%.

Capex estimates of about $12 million for the US plant and $4 million for Saudi Arabia; about $3 million already held as deposits in the US; the rest from internal accruals and debt (management expects debt of about $3-4 million); US banks reportedly willing to fund.
Data-centre pressure vessels: capacity of about 75-80 vessels a year in the existing Indore setup; management says a new plant may be needed if order flow is sustained.
Chennai plant ramp-up is still in progress; new production head moved there two weeks before the call.
demand_pricing: Pipeline: orders worth Rs72 crore already negotiated; a further Rs60 crore under negotiation; management expects about Rs72 crore more to be added in the current month.

Data-centre vessels: first order for 4 units; a 32-unit order under negotiation; more than 600 vessels quoted. Management says per-vessel value is Rs30-60 lakh and margins will be similar to other business.
US tariff: 15.6% currently (10% special tariff plus 5.6%); management is budgeting for 25% and says it will not price for 100%.
About 70% of US orders are to be made in America and 30% in India; management is cautious on new US order booking. A few large orders above $7 million each are under negotiation but not being pushed.
Mahr Maschinenbau (Austria): taking orders now, with manufacturing in UK and India; first jobs are 16 screens (2 for UK, 14 for Iraq); expected revenue about Rs15 crore per the presentation.
Competition in domestic water control gates and industrial process equipment: Tega, Delkor, Metso Minerals named as main competitors.

Singapore: a Rs6,000 crore figure discussed earlier was for project reports, not a bid; management says the overall Singapore investment is around Rs50,000-60,000 crore, spread over 15-20 years, and Jash's equipment is about 10% of project cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why was product-wise and region-wise breakup dropped from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IR team concluded order mix changes too much quarter to quarter, so data will be shown year-on-year going forward; a Q1 split of Rs70 crore India and Rs80 crore outside India was given.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q1 margin gain is from tariff refund versus manufacturing benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a combination; the Rs5.6 crore tariff refund was booked in consumption. Dharmendra Jain also said the revenue reversal for deferred March recognition (Rs27-28 crore) was offset in June, leaving about Rs10 crore positive.

qa_highlights.question: Rodney Hunt margin profile and path to 10% PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 40% of revenue is from old orders and 60% from new orders; expected PAT margin is 8-9%; 10% may be reached by FY28 if things go well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of Russia-sanctions/tariff risk and bidding in the US?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bidding continues but aggressive order-chasing has slowed; it will review after the next US visit, and a US Senate bill was cited as a risk.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Saudi and US plant timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi: approvals received, land application submitted, plant ready by December 2027 and operational by March 2028. US: land acquired, contractor to be finalised; both targeted in operation by March 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs875 crore FY27 target expected to be exceeded and what is executable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book of Rs932 crore is not all executable this year because some orders are deferred to FY28; there is scope to exceed Rs875 crore but it is too early to say.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Jash Process Equipment (WesTech) underperform?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said costing systems differed from what was expected at acquisition and marketing was not aggressive; a two-to-three-quarter transition is needed to set a clear direction.

risks_watch: US tariff and Russia-sanctions bill: management is budgeting 25% against the current 15.6%, has slowed aggressive order-chasing, and is not pricing for 100%; a US Senate bill was cited as a live risk.

Middle East shipments: Rs15 crore of Qatar, Singapore and Middle East material held back (Qatar stuck for over three months; Red Sea route closed after Houthi attacks); Singapore payment dispute on a particular client.
Jash Process Equipment (ex-WesTech): order book only Rs29 crore after Rs150-200 crore of orders lost in three to four months; full review under way, with a two-to-three-quarter transition.
Order book conversion: Rs932 crore order book is not fully executable in FY27 as some orders are deferred to FY28; Rs875 crore target depends on Rs72 crore pipeline additions this month.
Rodney Hunt: Q1 described as a weak quarter ('first quarter blues'); 8-9% PAT margin path to 10% depends on geopolitics; monitor Q2 and Q3 execution.

Tariff refund pipeline: further Rs7.5 crore refund pending legal vetting, expected in FY27; US and Saudi plant timelines (Saudi land by end CY2026, US contractor not yet finalised) and funding mix (about $3-4 million debt).
key_quotes: So, I would say overall the quarter has been satisfactory, not as much as I would have desired, but it is still much better than what we were last year.
Bidding has not been slowed down, but aggressively trying to get orders has been slowed down because the situation is so alarming that if something goes wrong, we spoil the margin.
Whenever you acquire a new company, we always think everything is very rosy at the time of acquisition.
And so, with that on positive note, I will say that we would meet our projections given earlier, which is Rs.875 crore with around Rs.100-105 crore profit after tax for the year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full year: management reiterated Rs875 crore revenue and Rs100-105 crore PAT and called the year 'quite bullish'. It was cautious and defensive on the US market, Russia-sanctions and tariff risk, Rodney Hunt margins, and the Jash Process Equipment underperformance, and it avoided giving firm numbers on FY27 upside or the 10% Rodney Hunt PAT timing.
